items.q: How are very unreactive metals like gold found in nature?
items.correct: Native — uncombined as the metal itself.
items.misconception: As compounds in ores, like reactive metals.
items.why: Unreactive metals occur uncombined; reactive metals are found as compounds and must be extracted.

items.q: Which metal wins a displacement reaction?
items.correct: The more reactive metal displaces the less reactive one.
items.misconception: The less reactive metal displaces the more reactive one.
items.why: A more reactive metal pushes a less reactive metal out of its compound (predicted by the reactivity series).

items.q: Do all metals react the same way with water?
items.correct: No — reactivity varies, from violent (potassium) to none (gold).
items.misconception: Yes, all metals react violently with water.
items.random_wrong: No metal ever reacts with acid.
items.why: The reactivity series ranks metals; reactions range from explosive to none at all.
